treaty_name: Convention between the United Kingdom and Algeria for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion and tax fraud with respect to taxes on income and on capital (2015)
eif_quote: [HMRC note in treaty PDF] ...entered into force on 16 June 2016. Article 27 of the Convention gives the dates on which the treaty enters into effect in each country, which will be: In Algeria: 1 January 2017 for withholding taxes and other taxes; In the United Kingdom: 1 January 2017 for withholding taxes
source_title: HMRC: Algeria-UK Double Taxation Convention (Algiers, 18 February 2015) – in force

rates.quote: a) 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner is a company (other than a partnership) which holds directly at least 25 per cent of the capital of the company paying the dividends;
b) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases.
but if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 7 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.
but if the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.basis: treaty arts. 10(6), 11(8), 12(7) (article-specific main purpose rules, not a general PPT)
ppt.quote: 6. No relief shall be available under this Article if it was the main purpose or one of the main purposes of any person concerned with the creation or assignment of the shares or other rights in respect of which the dividend is paid to take advantage of this Article by means of that creation or assignment.

notes: Effective for WHT from 1 January 2017 in both States (Art. 27; EIF 16-06-2016). Interest exclusive to residence State (Art. 11(3)) when beneficial owner is the State/central bank/subdivision, interest paid by the source State, or loans owed to/made/guaranteed/insured by the other State or its export financing agency. Main-purpose anti-abuse rules in Arts. 10(6), 11(8), 12(7) and 20(5); no general PPT; no MLI (Algeria not ratified).
